transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Martinez (Redwood Solutions), Mark Rivera (AuroraCloud Head of Platform), Sofia Lin (AuroraCloud Cloud Eng), Danielle Park (Aurora Partnerships), Omar Haddad (Aurora Security)

Summary:
- Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for Redwood on AuroraCloud marketplace, and joint solution play for private + dedicated deployments.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to produce marketplace draft, reference-arch repo and helm chart stub; Aurora to provide test account + security docs.

Topics covered: marketplace listing metadata, billing & SKUs, reference architecture (VPC, Private deployment, Dedicated pool), auth/integration (SSO/SAML, IAM roles), KMS/encryption, operator/helm install experience, SLAs & support, joint pilot timeline.

Transcript:  
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - um, appreciate the time. This is Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya and Luis from the solutions eng team.
[00:10] Mark Rivera: Hey Alex, thanks. Mark here, uh, Head of Platform at AuroraCloud. Sophie - sorry, Sofia - and Omar are on. Danielle's on for partner ops.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya, Redwood SE. Today we want to run through the marketplace listing checklist, the reference architecture we had sketched, and then dig into any security or deployment asks you have.
[00:30] Sofia Lin: Sounds good, thanks. Our main priorities - quick one: marketplace listing needs to pass AuroraCloud's vetting (images, IaC, docs), and we want a clear reference-arch for our customers to deploy Redwood Private in their VPCs.
[00:42] Luis Martinez: Perfect. We'll show the high-level diagram and then discuss the helm/operator options.
[00:48] Mark Rivera: Also want to confirm the partner pricing model - does Redwood expect per-token billing through our marketplace, or do we need a dedicated billing contract for reserved capacity?
[00:58] Alex Chen: Good question. We support both. For marketplace we can do a metered offering (per-token) or a reserved commit SKU that maps to Redwood Dedicated. We'll include both in the draft listing so Aurora can choose which to promote.
[01:12] Danielle Park: Do you have standard SKUs you use for Dedicated? Our marketplace requires a SKU catalog for each offer.
[01:18] Alex Chen: Yes - Priya, can you call out the SKU approach?
[01:21] Priya Nair: Sure - typically we publish 3 SKUs: hosted metered, dedicated small (x GPUs / reserved throughput), and dedicated large. Each SKU will link to a support/ops onboarding doc. We'll provide the SKU ids in the draft.
[01:34] Mark Rivera: Cool. On to the reference architecture - can you show the diagram?
[01:38] Priya Nair: Yeah, pulling up the architecture we sketched. (brief pause) So top left is AuroraCloud marketplace storefront, customer clicks deploy - that triggers a marketplace flow which can either provision a Redwood-managed hosted integration, or a customer-managed Private deployment into their VPC. For Private we recommend a Helm-based operator that creates pods for the Redwood runtime, with NLB in front; we also include KMS integration for key management and an option to plug in Aurora's KMS.
[02:10] Sofia Lin: When you say "Redwood runtime" is that the same binary for Dedicated and Private or do you have separate images?
[02:17] Priya Nair: Same core runtime but slightly different packaging. Hosted uses our managed control plane, Dedicated uses a variant tuned for reserved capacity and autoscaling, Private deploys are containerized with config flags for private telemetry and customer KMS. There can be confusion in naming - sometimes folks think it's multiple services but it's mainly variants of the same runtime.
[02:38] Mark Rivera: Right, and for our buyers we need clear docs on network requirements: ports, subnets, egress to Redwood control plane (if they opt into managed control plane), and an offline on-prem option for air-gapped customers.
[02:52] Priya Nair: We'll include a network checklist: ports 443 for control-plane and model pull, optional gRPC ports for intra-cluster comms, and guidance on NAT/firewall. For air-gapped we provide an image bundle + install script but that requires an enterprise agreement.
[03:07] Omar Haddad: On encryption - we need details on KMS and key lifecycle. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys and AWS KMS and HSM?
[03:16] Alex Chen: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we encrypt at rest and can use a CMK for enterprise customers. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[03:29] Omar Haddad: Great. Also SOC2 evidence - do you have the report we can share with our compliance team?
[03:34] Priya Nair: We do - we'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs. Expecting to share them under an NDA if needed.
[03:40] Danielle Park: Marketplace vetting often flags images that run as root - do you have non-root images?
[03:46] Priya Nair: Yes we publish non-root images and we'll include a note in the repo. The Helm chart values will default to non-root user and limited fs access.
[03:54] Mark Rivera: On the operator/helm - do you maintain the operator, or is Aurora expected to package it for the marketplace?
[04:00] Luis Martinez: Redwood will publish the helm chart repo and maintain releases; Aurora's marketplace will reference the chart. We can also publish an operator that makes upgrades easier.
[04:10] Sofia Lin: For upgrades, is there a recommended strategy to avoid KV cache warmup problems? We worried about performance regressions when switching versions.
[04:18] Priya Nair: Good catch - we recommend rolling upgrades with canary traffic. The runtime supports KV cache pre-warming strategies; plus we have a graceful fallback to previous model variants to avoid regression. We'll document the rollout steps in the reference arch.
[04:34] Mark Rivera: Nice. About telemetry - what does Redwood collect by default? We need to ensure PII is not sent to Redwood control plane for Private deployments.
[04:44] Alex Chen: For Private deployments telemetry is minimal by default: metrics and anonymized errors. No PII. If a customer opts into managed control-plane we can collect more telemetry but only after opt-in. We'll include the exact list in the security appendix.
[04:58] Omar Haddad: And audit logs? We need request-level audit for enterprise customers.
[05:03] Priya Nair: We provide audit logs (request ids, timestamps, token usage) that can be pushed to customer S3/Azure blob or forwarded to SIEM. We'll detail retention and log formats.
[05:15] Mark Rivera: On the marketplace listing itself - Aurora needs screenshots, a short description, a long description, billing SKUs, a support contact, and a set of install scripts. Can you provide those?
[05:26] Alex Chen: Yes - we'll prepare a listing pack: logos (SVG/PNG), short/long descriptions, screenshots of Console, sample customer success stories (sanitized), and the install artifacts.
[05:36] Danielle Park: Timeline - our process usually takes 2-3 weeks for vetting after submission. If we get the initial package by 3/24 can we aim to publish in April?
[05:44] Mark Rivera: (interject) depends on security review; but reasonable.
[05:47] Alex Chen: We'll prioritize the listing pack and the reference-arch repo. Priya will own the repo.
[05:52] Priya Nair: I'll create a public/private repo depending on your preference. For now, we'll create a partners repo in Redwood's org and add AuroraCloud as a collaborator so you can review the charts.
[06:04] Sofia Lin: Prefer private until vetting is complete.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Private repo then.
[06:08] Mark Rivera: For the joint solution messaging - do you have a joint solution one-pager and a reference-arch PDF we can co-brand?
[06:15] Luis Martinez: We can provide a one-pager and a slide deck. We'll mock up co-branding options and share in the repo.
[06:22] Mark Rivera: Ok. A couple technical nitty-gritty items: container image sizes - we need to know whether the runtime image is >10GB - marketplace restricts very large images.
[06:31] Priya Nair: The base runtime is ~3.5GB compressed, model artifacts are separate and pulled at runtime; we provide slimmed images for marketplace use that are under 1GB, and model pulls occur post-deploy. We'll add size numbers to the listing pack.
[06:44] Sofia Lin: How do you handle model updates? Customers with Private deployments pull models from Redwood registries?
[06:50] Priya Nair: They can pull from a Redwood model registry (authenticated). For on-prem/offline we provide model bundles that they can host in a local store. Updates are opt-in or can be automated based on deployment policy.
[07:02] Omar Haddad: About identity - SSO for the console, and for API calls should customers use IAM roles or token-based integration?
[07:10] Alex Chen: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) for the console, and for APIs we support token-based auth and role-based access via IAM integration for Private deployments. The recommended approach is SSO for humans and short-lived tokens for service-to-service with role scoping.
[07:25] Mark Rivera: Any known blockers for Aurora's marketplace cert tests?
[07:28] Danielle Park: The main ones are non-root images, SBOM, license info, and a reference-arch that shows networking.
[07:35] Priya Nair: We'll include SBOM, license, non-root confirmation, and a network checklist with example terraform for the VPC.
[07:44] Mark Rivera: Great. On billing flow for a reserved commit SKU - do you require billing-proxy or can we route billing through Aurora's marketplace?
[07:52] Alex Chen: We can support marketplace-brokered billing via Aurora's billing; alternatively a direct contract with a pass-through is possible. We'll work with Aurora's finance/partners team on the preferred model.
[08:04] Luis Martinez: For pilot tests, we typically run a 2-week POC: baseline latency/throughput benchmarks (10k tokens/day or similar), and provide a tuning plan (batching, quantization suggestions) via Redwood Optimize.
[08:17] Sofia Lin: Perfect. We'll need a quick reference for the tests so our infra team can spin up probes.
[08:22] Priya Nair: I'll add benchmark scripts to the repo (a simple loadgen with perf metrics).
[08:27] Mark Rivera: Anything else on infra?
[08:30] Omar Haddad: One more: data residency. Some customers require model inference to remain in-region. Does Redwood support region pinning for Dedicated/Private?
[08:39] Alex Chen: Yes - Dedicated pools can be region-specific; Private is deployed in-customer region by definition. For hosted multi-region we have routing policies to keep inference in-region. We'll document these constraints.
[08:52] Danielle Park: Last question: marketing approvals - do you need our legal to sign a co-marketing agreement?
[08:57] Alex Chen: Yes, for joint logos and case studies we'll need a simple MSA amendment / co-marketing addendum. We'll send a draft after this call.
[09:06] Mark Rivera: Great. Thanks all.
[09:09] Alex Chen: Recap of agreed next steps - Alex to send listing pack by 3/24, Priya will create private repo and push reference-arch + helm stub by 3/26, Aurora to provide test account and security contact by 3/25, schedule pilot kickoff week of 4/6.
[09:30] Sofia Lin: Sounds good.
[09:32] Danielle Park: Thanks, looking forward.
[09:34] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email and attach the docs.

Notes about transcript quality: some names slightly mis-transcribed (Luis occasionally flagged as "Lewis") and minor recognition issues (K V cache was sometimes transcribed as K-V cash).

References / attachments mentioned: 
- Redwood marketplace listing draft (to be shared)
- Reference-arch repo (private, invite AuroraCloud)
- Security whitepaper and SOC2 attestation (attach after NDA)
- Helm chart stub and benchmark scripts (in repo)

End of transcript.
